fact: Law Lab Africa states that no comprehensive data protection law is in force in Eritrea, as of a verification pass on 1 August 2026.
Law Lab Africa states that no supervisory authority has been established in Eritrea, as of 1 August 2026.
Law Lab Africa states that no enforcement decisions could be found for Eritrea and none are published, as of the 1 August 2026 verification pass.
Law Lab Africa's dossier updated 1 August 2026 records Eritrea's data protection position as unchanged: no law, no regulator and no enforcement.

The Horn of Africa Initiative Digital Policy Matrix update (June 2025, World Bank team) states that Eritrea remains at a nascent stage without data protection legislation, unlike Kenya, Somalia and Ethiopia which have enacted frameworks.

The Horn of Africa Initiative Digital Policy Matrix update (June 2025) states that Eritrea remains without regulatory oversight for data protection, while Kenya, Somalia and Ethiopia have established supervisory authorities.

The UNECA Digital Trade Regulatory Integration country profile states that Eritrea lacks a comprehensive legal framework for data protection; the document gives no date, so its published year 2022 is used (its datasets cover measures collected through 2021).
